info.name: @Coalesce POC — with vs without
info.description:
A/B load test for the @Coalesce framework.

HOW TO RUN
1. Start the app and Redis, then send '00 Reset metrics' once.
2. Collection Runner -> select the folder 'A - WITHOUT coalescing'.
   Iterations: 200+, and raise the runner's concurrency if available.
3. Run the folder 'B - WITH coalescing' with the SAME iteration count.
   Equal request counts is what makes the comparison fair.
4. Send '99 Report' and read the console output.

Newman:
  newman run postman/coalesce-poc.postman_collection.json \
    --folder 'A - WITHOUT coalescing' -n 200
  newman run postman/coalesce-poc.postman_collection.json \
    --folder 'B - WITH coalescing' -n 200
  newman run postman/coalesce-poc.postman_collection.json --folder Report

Both folders hit the same endpoint with the same work behind it; only the
'coalesce' flag differs, so the gap in downstream executions is the saving.

VARIABLES
  keyCount  distinct coalescing keys the load spreads over (default 10).
            Raise it to model high-cardinality traffic; the saving falls off fast
            once requests-per-key-per-freshTtl drops near 1.
  maxOrders must match demo.max-orders in application.yaml (default 25). The server
            caps response size independently of the bucket range, so the length
            assertion expects min(bucket, maxOrders).

item.description: Baseline: every request reaches the downstream. Run with N iterations.

request.description: Bypasses @Coalesce entirely. Executions will equal requests.

exec: // How many distinct coalescing keys the load spreads over. Low values mean many
// virtual users collide on one key, which is what coalescing collapses. Raise it to
// model high-cardinality traffic, where there is nothing to share and the saving
// 503 is expected for roughly 5% of calls: the downstream's slow tail.
// The server caps the order count at demo.max-orders, independently of the bucket
// range, so the expected length is min(bucket, maxOrders) rather than bucket.
// Keep maxOrders here in step with demo.max-orders in application.yaml.

item.name: B - WITH coalescing
item.description: Same endpoint and same downstream, through @Coalesce. Use the SAME N.

request.description: Concurrent callers on one bucket share a single execution; results are then cached for freshTtl (2s) and refreshed in the background while stale.

request.description: Side-by-side comparison. Read the Postman console for the summary table.

exec: const d = s.direct, c = s.coalesced, cmp = s.comparison;
console.log('  without coalesce   ' + String(d.requests).padEnd(11) + String(d.downstreamExecutions).padEnd(12) + d.executionsSaved);
console.log('  with coalesce      ' + String(c.requests).padEnd(11) + String(c.downstreamExecutions).padEnd(12) + c.executionsSaved);
console.log('  executions per request    : ' + cmp.directExecutionsPerRequest + ' -> ' + cmp.coalescedExecutionsPerRequest + ' (' + cmp.timesFewerExecutions + ' fewer)');
console.log('  framework                 : leader=' + s.framework.leaderExecutions + ' cacheHits=' + s.framework.cacheHits + ' waits=' + s.framework.followerWaits);
